title: Release baseline consolidation
objective: Consolidate only reviewed release-critical changes onto the dense QQ release authority and publish a validated release candidate source branch without tagging or publishing artifacts

oracles: Existing portable, strict-Python, native compiler, and release policy suites

runs.command: node --test test/linux-release-baseline.cjs test/sea-build-manifest.cjs test/release-candidate-linux.cjs test/release-artifact-acceptance.cjs test/test-manifest.test.cjs

handoff.summary: Closed the independently reviewed intermediate release checkpoint after integrating the portable compiler fixes, Linux x64/arm64 glibc baseline and SEA authority, complete cross-platform artifact acceptance and licensing authority, Linux Node 26.7 Temporal/Rust source authority, macOS ZeroMQ source authority, and isolated prime host benchmarks. The current combined release-focused suite, architecture gate, and all-contract gate pass at 388f8cc7c72659bd9e51bf061ca3bced01f80092.
risks: This is an intermediate source checkpoint, not the frozen release commit: first-party macOS packaging/signing workflow and canonical unsigned Windows packaging remain active reviewed lanes.
Native x64, arm64, macOS, and Windows final artifacts must still be rebuilt and accepted from the eventual frozen commit.
next_steps: Rebase the shared FFLAS cache expectation and macOS workflow lanes on this closed checkpoint so their task claims can pass independently.
Complete and integrate macOS before rebasing the Windows lane, then open a new narrow final-integration contract only after both child claim sets are inactive.
